stories.title: Rhino Dung Paper Is How This Family Makes Money and Protects These Amazing Animals
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: A father and daughter in India have found a clever way to turn rhino dung into paper and stationery. Local villagers collect the dung, so they earn money from it. Villagers who once might have clashed with rhinos now see the animals as a steady source of income. That gives them a real reason to protect these magnificent creatures, and the paper is a lovely product too.
stories.why_good: A working business is paying local people and giving them a reason to protect rhinos, so both the families and the animals benefit.

stories.title: Every Tuesday, This Chef Cooks for 100 People in Need Using Random Food Bank Ingredients
stories.label: people
stories.summary: Toronto-area chef Maddy Goldberg has spent years giving her Tuesdays to cook for people who need a good meal. Each week she prepares banquet-style, made-from-scratch dishes for 100 guests. She builds the menu from whatever ingredients the food bank happens to have, turning a mixed bag of groceries into something special. She also shares her recipes on social media, where her warmth makes the food look even more inviting.
stories.why_good: A real, ongoing weekly program that puts hundreds of hot, thoughtfully made meals in front of people who need them, and treats them as honored guests.
